newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN HAS NO COMMENT ON PROPERTY SALE PRICE.
newsitem.headline: GAN HAS NO COMMENT ON PROPERTY SALE PRICE.

text.p: French state-controlled insurer GAN said on Monday it could not comment on a report in business daily Les Echos that it had got 675 million francs for a package of distressed real estate.

GAN announced late on Friday it had sold the portfolio, which carried a gross value of three billion francs, to U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley and Constructa, a property firm headquartered in Paris and Miami.
In the Friday announcement, GAN gave no price for the deal, part of its ongoing drive to dig itself out of a long-running property slump as its gears up for privatisation.
Some 75 buildings were covered by the auction, the first big sale of a portfolio of buildings rather than property loans. The deal is expected to pave the way for similar transactions.

"It's the first time these assets sold from these discounted portfolios have been put on the market. It's the type of operation we are going to see in the coming years," said Donald Bryden, Bankers Trust France managing director, which handled the auction.
